items.title: Final Fantasy XIV's Naoki Yoshida Comments on Difficulties of Remaking Final Fantasy IV, VIII, IX
items.content:
Yoshi-P's comments came after Final Fantasy VII Remake series director Naoki Hamaguchi was asked about a game that had a lasting impression or influence on him. Hamaguchi notes he has said in interviews Final Fantasy VI is a game that had the biggest impact on his life. However, he further states media outlets have blown his answer out of proportion and claim “Hamaguchi is remaking Final Fantasy VI”, to which the Final Fantasy VII Remake series director always refutes.

The Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival in Berlin took place at the Messe Berlin, hub27 between July 25-26. The next Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival is set to take place at the Makuhari Messe on October 31-November 1.

The Fan Fest revealed a collaboration with Final Fantasy VII Remake for its Normal Raids in the "Evercold" expansion for Square Enix 's Final Fantasy XIV MMORPG. The event also unveiled the new Tank job "Bastion."

Final Fantasy VII Rebirth , the sequel to Final Fantasy VII Remake , debuted worldwide in February 2024 on two discs for PlayStation 5. The game then launched on PC via Steam and Epic Games Store in January 2025, and then launched for Nintendo Switch 2 on June 3. The final game in the Rebirth trilogy Final Fantasy VII Revelation will launch next spring.

Sources: Final Fantasy XIV series' YouTube channel , Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival's website via Hachima Kikō

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 could finally introduce a controversial feature to welcome new players
items.summary: Square Enix is finally considering making the hundreds of hours of story easier for new players
items.content:
Listen Thread 2 Add Us Link copied to clipboard By Willa Rowe Published Jul 29, 2026, 2:49 PM EDT News Producer Naoki Yoshida says the team is considering ways to make the lengthy story easier

FFXIV Evercold will finally modernize some of the MMO's most outdated features Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's director can't promise a physical release, but he wants it Despite Magic's unprecedented success, Wizards' president is already stepping down Final Fantasy 14 could finally introduce a controversial feature to welcome new players Photo: Square Enix Final Fantasy 14 Sign in to your Polygon.com account It is becoming increasingly difficult to recommend Final Fantasy 14 to new players as the years go on. Now in its 13th year of service with a sixth expansion due in January, the MMORPG requires hundreds of hours to complete — and that's if we are just talking about the main story. Despite this Herculean effort, Square Enix has been adamant that players must go through the entire game's story to access the latest content. That could finally be changing.

During a media Q&A at Final Fantasy Fan Fest in Berlin (as reported by PC Gamer ), Final Fantasy 14 producer Naoki Yoshida revealed the development team is working on potential solutions to make the game more accessible to beginners. "I had previously said that I want players to enjoy the story, so I would like them to have a fresh experience right from A Realm Reborn ," Yoshida admitted "But now we are at this point, we've begun thinking about accommodating these kinds of requests."

Yoshida shared that Square Enix is considering two ways to address the issue, though he remained fairly cryptic on both. He said that the first one will be implemented before or at Evercold 's release. He teased that the second solution involves a system whose feasibility the development team is in the process of reviewing. "There's a non-zero possibility of us being able to implement it for [patch] 8.0. So there is a possibility that we could make it," Yoshida said.

While the topic of a streamlined path or skip through Final Fantasy 14 's story remains controversial among the fanbase, it makes sense for Square Enix to consider it at this point in the MMO's life. Evercold , the game's next expansion, marks the start of the Godless Realms Saga. This is something of a new beginning, with the MMO's initial story wrapping up in 2021's Endwalker . It has the potential to be the perfect onboarding point for beginners who have, until now, been intimidated by the game's mountain of quests.

Square Enix has already trimmed the lengthy list of main scenario quests over the years in an attempt to make catching up with Final Fantasy 14 easier, but even this has failed to keep pace with the volume of new story content each expansion adds. There are paid story skips available to players for each expansion, but Square Enix seems ready to consider a free implementation of something similar going forward.

One of the biggest concerns with offering players the ability to jump right in to the latest expansion is how it will affect the rest of the player-base. While the story is important, the hours of playtime it takes to get through it also help players learn just how Final Fantasy 14 's mechanics work. As content still revolves around teaming up with other players, 'the community worries that an influx of players without proper tutorials could harm everyone's experience. Yoshida hinted that more details on potential solutions could come during Tokyo Fan Fest in October.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14′ s Next Expansion Will Feature A Crossover With Final Fantasy 7 So Of Course Fans Are Gonna Fight About It
items.summary: Am I tired of FF7? Yes. Am I still gonna try raiding for the first time just to see this content? Also yes.
items.content:
The conclusion of the Final Fantasy XIV Fan Fest in Berlin brought with it a lot of new updates for Evercold , the game’s upcoming expansion due in January of next year. We got new information on one of the expansion’s two new classes, more details on the story and tweaks to the game’s battle and questing systems, and all the ways players will be able to customize their characters because of course, glamour is the endgame. And one particular announcement—that Evercold ‘s raid series will be a crossover with Final Fantasy VII Remake— has the fandom up in arms.

Presenting a FINAL FANTASY XIV x FINAL FANTASY VII Remake crossover: Beyond the Lifestream—the Evercold raid series developed in collaboration with @finalfantasyvii ! pic.twitter.com/wzkPKFpQky

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@FF_XIV_EN) July 25, 2026

On the one hand, I get it. Final Fantasy fans have been inundated with this one iteration of Square Enix’s storied franchise for decades now, even before the remake trilogy kicked off back in 2020. And as exciting as that remake trilogy is, I’m kinda tired of seeing Cloud’s ass, too. If I played Final Fantasy XIV to get away from all that, I’d be pissed like some fans are.

Having both raid series be crossovers is very overkill. Why must i go and watch a boring anime and a play 3 new RPG games costing upwards of £150 total to understand the raids in my MMO?

I hope the expansion after Evercold has 2 original raid series to make up for this!

— 「 Xavier Maganti 」 (@JamieCharlesEl1) July 25, 2026

Collabing on BOTH raid types right at the start of what is supposed to be a new storyline is definitely a choice What a wasted opportunity to start adding new lore pic.twitter.com/m2gXqK8WPq

— 🗡️🐍RedPanda 🇪🇭 🇵🇸 (@Surgiote) July 25, 2026

People are saying folks who don't dig this should shut up because XIV is full of references, but no other game in this franchise is pushed remotely as much as VII is. It's reasonable for some people to not be hyped for more.

And man… not everything has to be an argument. It's just opinions.

— Bex (@bexthecat.bsky.social) 2026-07-25T15:26:16.645Z

There’s also a lingering sentiment among players that holding a crossover with the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy now (rather than having one earlier in the trilogy’s lifecycle) is a sly attempt to win back lapsed players or earn new ones who are in the FF ecosystem but never dabbled in the MMO. A lot of players checked out of the game during Dawntrail , the most recent expansion whose story was just not as strong as those of previous expansions (following up Endwalker was always gonna be tough) and adding stuff from the big daddy Final Fantasy entry to the MMO certainly feels like an “in case of emergency, break glass” scenario.

And it’s almost certainly gonna work, too, because for as much as I don’t wanna see Sephiroth’s 34-inch white-blonde buss down on my screen anymore, I will show up for a chance to hear composer Masayoshi Soken’s take on One Winged Angel.

items.title: New FFXIV Twitch Support-a-Streamer Mount Is a Unicorn
items.summary: The FFXIV Twitch Support-a-Streamer promotion is back and this time Alsvid the unicorn mount is the reward.
items.content:
Square Enix announced a new Twitch Support-a-Streamer FFXIV promotion that gives players a chance to buy and gift qualifying subscriptions in order to earn an Alsvid Whistle to summon a new rainbow unicorn mount. It kicked off on July 28, 2026. People will have until August 25, 2026 to earn the Mog Station code for the item, and they need to have an active account to redeem the code.

The Twitch promotion only applies to streams in the FFXIV category on the service and Affiliate and Partner channels streaming the game while that stream is set to the correct category. You then need to buy three subscriptions. These can be tier 1, 2, or 3 ones that you either get for yourself or choose to gift.

After you buy the three applicable subscriptions, you will get the FFXIV Alsvid unicorn mount code in your Twitch Notifications Inbox. Only one code can be earned per promotion. Said Item Code can be redeemed in Mog Station in Registration Codes.

To go along with the reveal, Square Enix also shared two in-game screenshots of the mount being used.

This sort of FFXIV Twitch Support-a-Streamer promotion happened before. In 2024, it ended up being the way to get the Snowstreamer Snowman mount.

Final Fantasy XIV is on the PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC now, comes to the Switch 2 on August 4, 2026, and FFXIV Evercold will appear in January 2027. The FFXIV Twitch Support-a-Streamer Alsvid the unicorn mount promotion will run between July 28, 2026 and August 25, 2026.

Final Fantasy 14 Will Be The Nintendo Switch 2's Biggest Game by Install Size
items.summary: Square Enix MMO Final Fantasy 14 will land on Switch 2 with an almighty thud next month, as its honking install size will take up almost half of the console's 256GB memory.
items.content:
Square Enix MMO Final Fantasy 14 will land on Switch 2 with an almighty thud next month, as its honking install size will take up almost half of the console's 256GB memory.

Final Fantasy 14 will weigh in at 117.2GB when it launches for Switch 2 on August 4, an eShop listing for the title has now revealed. Here's hoping you have space for it — or the budget to buy a new SD card.

That's around double the game's install size on PlayStation 5, which benefits from some clever file compression technology, though similar to the game's memory footprint on PC. It's a hefty download, though perhaps to be expected when you consider the MMO's size and the amount of content that has been added over the years.

The upside to all this is that the filesize includes all of the game's previous five expansions — Heavensward, Stormblood, Shadowbringers, Endwalker and Dawntrail — so you won't need more space to play any of those. The downside? A sixth expansion, Evercold, is already on the way — meaning you'll likely need even more memory space from next January.

Somewhat amusingly, Final Fantasy publisher Square Enix is no stranger to holding the record for the biggest Switch 2 games by memory size. Until the launch of Final Fantasy 14, Square Enix's Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth holds the current record (91.8GB) for a single game, as well as the record for a game bundle (the Kingdom Hearts Collection, which includes a trio of titles that weigh in at 131GB total).

Final Fantasy 14 game director Naoki Yoshida suited up in Bastion armor to take the stage at Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin to confirm the title's long-awaited Switch 2 launch date over the weekend, alongside a laundry list of new updates coming in the near future . The game's first month on sale will be offered without any subscription charge as its servers are stabilized. After this period comes to an end, players will be required to purchase a subscription as normal.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Evercold's new DPS job will be revealed in October, but Square Enix is already dropping some big, feathered hints
items.summary: Stay tuned for Fan Fest in Japan, then
items.content:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Square Enix) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Square Enix plans to reveal the next Final Fantasy 14 DPS job in a few months from now, and some fresh clues already have fans fawning over the possibility of playing as a bird-loving Falconer-type when the game's Evercold expansion drops.

This past weekend, Final Fantasy 14 composer and sound designer Masayoshi Soken took to the Fan Fest stage in Berlin to tease fans with two audio snippets related to the unannounced second job coming in next year's Evercold expansion, alongside the Bastion .

The first snippet blasted clinging and clanging noises at the audience, while the second sounded like a bird screeching and clawing at something. You can try to decipher the clues for yourself in the clip below.

"These are sound effects from the new DPS job we're going to announce at the JP Fan Fest," it's revealed via a translator. The Japanese leg of Fan Fest is set to begin on October 31, 2026, so we won't need to wait too much longer to find out what the team's been cooking.

Over on Reddit, theorists are overwhelmingly in agreement that all clues are pointing to a Falconer job or something adjacent to that, at least (Hunter, Ranger, Beastmaster, etc.) "Falconer is the ranged DPS we saw in the trailer. Bet," one fan writes .

The Bastion is Final Fantasy 14's first new job for Evercold, a hulking tank with a shield and gun on each arm Final Fantasy 14 Evercold sleuths think they've figured out the MMO's new jobs The Final Fantasy 7 Remake series comes to Final Fantasy 14 as part of an Evercold raid Evercold's extended teaser trailer threw fuel over the fire, too, with a brief glimpse of a large, armored, winged creature taking flight and annoying a spellcaster.

Watch On "Willing to bet that the bird in the trailer is related to the job, but the girl is unrelated," another theorycrafter says . "The last trailer will likely extend that shot to show the bird flying to whoever is our job representative! The baton she has is more likely a plot device, rather than the weapon of the job."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

A Falconer job would be entirely new for the Final Fantasy series, though past games have dabbled with similar concepts. Final Fantasy 10-2's Trainer job gives one of the characters a big bird to command, for example. And Final Fantasy 5's Hunter can also occasionally call in help from woodland critters, flying types included.

items.title: Wisdom of Nym: Reactions to Final Fantasy XIV’s second fan festival
Yoshi-P says his approach to development on FF14 "hasn't really changed" since A Realm Reborn
Final Fantasy 14 comes to Switch 2 later this year with the now-famous free trial, but the file size is going to be absolutely massive
items.summary: Evercold, the next FF14 expansion, is coming in early 2027, but Square Enix is making a splash this summer with a Switch 2 port of the MMO.
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer / Square Enix / Nintendo News by Fran Ruiz Contributor Published on July 27, 2026 7 comments Follow Final Fantasy XIV: Online One of this year's most surprising Nintendo Switch 2 port announcements was Final Fantasy 14's back in April , and against all expectations, it was set to arrive in August. Now we know it's right around the corner, and the Evercold expansion has received a big teaser trailer, too.

During the Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin , a five-minute 'extended teaser trailer' that sets the stage for the MMORPG's next chapter - the start of the Godless Realms Saga story arc - was shown alongside plenty of fresh details. Perhaps the most important one was the reveal of the Bastion , a new tank class "that wields a pair of greatshields known as skyltborg".

Pre-orders for the Switch 2 version of the game, which is confirmed to launch on 4th August, were also opened. As a reminder, the ambitious port will require a separate monthly sub from the other versions of the game even if you're using the same account, but it won't require the usual Nintendo Switch Online membership that online games typically ask for. Those willing to pay two different FF14 subs will get a 50 percent discount on the Switch 2 one, though.

The better news is that FF14 on Switch 2 will also have the popular free trial - which includes quite a bit of content - in order to entice players who are on the fence. That said, anyone who's looking to jump into the MMO on Nintendo's hybrid console will need to liberate - according to the US eShop - 117.2 GB at launch. It'll no doubt be one of Switch 2's largest games, but if we look at FF7 Remake and Rebirth hovering around 90 GB, it seems more than reasonable for a massive MMO with a ridiculous amount of content.

Other Final Fantasy 14 reveals that came this past weekend include an Evangelion 'Ghosts of Desire' collaboration, the announcement of a new data centre system for improved connectivity and same-region player matching, and a planned crossover with the FF7 Remake trilogy .
